_about: How many people were alive, from the oldest bones of our kind, about 315,000 years ago, to now, with a band and a log scale (CWVault/claude/Plots-Deep-01.md, People, 9 Oct 2026). From 10,000 BCE the values are those of stories/curves/people.json (Our World in Data); before that, eight points that are a guess made for Curious Woods: people alive, not breeding ancestors, and where a genetic number is used it is multiplied by 3 to 10. Built 22 Nov 2026 and read by the Time Machine (active/time-machine.html). Each point [year, people, low, high]; year is the store's astronomer's year. Made by tools/curves-deep-time.py.

source.citation: Our World in Data, “Population – HYDE, Gapminder, UN – Long-run data” [dataset], fetched 30 Sep 2026 from ourworldindata.org/grapher/population (World). Underlying: PBL Netherlands Environmental Assessment Agency, HYDE 3.3 (2023); Gapminder, Population v7 (2022); United Nations, World Population Prospects (2024).

source.citation: United Nations, World Population Prospects 2024, medium projection: about 8.3 billion (low and high here 8.2 and 8.4 billion)

US Census Bureau, Historical Estimates of World Population, the low and high summaries: 10,000 BCE 1 to 10 million; 5000 BCE 5 to 20 million; 1 CE 170 to 400 million; 1000 CE 254 to 345 million; 1500 CE 425 to 540 million; 1800 CE 813 to 1,125 million; interpolated in log between them, narrowing to 2 percent either way at 1950 and after; opened where the fetched value lies outside it

Biraben, J.-N. (2003), L'évolution du nombre des hommes, Population & Sociétés 394 (perhaps 800,000 at 300,000 to 200,000 years; past a million between 40,000 and 30,000); Deevey (1960) as tabled by Kremer (1993) (1 million at 300,000 BCE, all humans, not our kind only; 3.34 million at 25,000 BCE); Li, H. & Durbin, R. (2011), Inference of human population history from individual whole-genome sequences, Nature (breeding numbers about 16,000 at 100,000 to 150,000 years; about 5,700 at 50,000, African ancestry); Tallavaara and others (2015) (Europe alone, about 330,000 at 30,000 years, about 130,000 at the glacial maximum); Smith and others (2018), against a bottleneck at the Toba eruption, 74,000 years ago; Frankham (1995): in wild animals, breeding numbers are about a tenth of all numbers

howSure: Shaky before farming: the range is a factor of ten to thirty before 50,000 years ago and about ten after, the spread between guesses from archaeology and estimates from genes. From 10,000 BCE reconstructions with wide ranges; after 1950 censuses, good to a few percent.
_range: from and to are the store years (astronomer's years) the curve is meaningful between — its first and last points; minPoints is the fewest points a period must hold for the curve to be offered (Prompt-Build-Timeline-Stack.md, part 6, 10 Oct 2026)
